summary: Petition under Section 62 and 79 (1) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with related provisions of the Chapter-5 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2003 and Regulation 27 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms & Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024 for approval of proposal for Renovation & Modernization for life extension beyond the normal useful life in respect of Khandong Power Station of NEEPCO Ltd. North Eastern Electric Power Corporation Limited Corporate Office: Brookland Compound Lower New Colony, Shillong 793 003, Meghalaya ** Petitioner** The Petitioner, North Eastern Electric Power Corporation Limited (in short ‘NEEPCO’), 3. The Petitioner had earlier filed Petition No. 633/MP/2020 before this Commission, seeking approval of the proposal for R&M for life extension, beyond the normal useful life in respect of KhPS (50 MW), after obtaining consent from the beneficiaries. The Petitioner has submitted that, based on the original DPR, against the R&M and life extension, approval of CEA was obtained on (i) Budget Estimate of EM and Civil Costs of R&M and LE of Khandong, (ii) Revised Installed capacity & Design Energy and (iii) Time Schedule & Phasing of hard cost. After the admission of the said petition by Commission, and after obtaining the in-principle approval of CEA, some enabling activities of R&M and LE were started by the Petitioner, which primarily comprised of (a) Urgent issues which need immediate attention such as Penstock Protection Butterfly Valves/ Emergency DG sets/ EOT Crane etc. and (b) Enabling activities to optimise generation during the R&M and LE such as Tunnel and Gate works. Further, while carrying out the enabling activities, KhPS was completely inundated by a flash flood, causing major damage to all the Electrical and Mechanical equipment, the Valve House, Steel Liner and the Y-Piece and the Power House Building. For cleaning of the debris, dismantling and removal of all damaged equipment took more than 13 months (till May 2023). However, the Commission vide its order dated 31.7.2025 disposed of the said petition, as ‘withdrawn’, as stated below: _“4. During the hearing of the Petition on 2.7.2025, the representative of the Petitioner made oral submissions in support of the reliefs sought in the petition. However, on a specific query of the Commission with regard to the status of approval of the DPR by the CEA, the representative of the Petitioner clarified that the DPR submitted to CEA for approval on 4.8.2020, is under active consideration by the CEA, and approval is expected shortly. On an observation of the Commission that no purpose would be served to keep the matter pending, considering the fact that the DPR approval by CEA is awaited and that the anticipated COD of the Units (post-R&M) would fall during the period 2024-29, thereby requiring revision of the petition in terms of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, the representative of the Petitioner sought permission to withdraw the present petition, with liberty to the Petitioner to approach the Commission on this subject, after approval of the DPR. He also prayed for adjustment of the filing fees paid for the present Petition, against the Petition to be filed on the subject, in future._ _5. In view of the above submissions, the Petitioner is permitted to ‘withdraw’ the present Petition with the liberty to approach the Commission in the future, with a fresh petition, along with all relevant supporting documents. The filing fees paid in the present Petition will be adjusted against the Petition to be filed in the future, as stated above._ 5. During the hearing of the petition on ‘admission’, the learned counsel for the Petitioner, made detailed oral submissions in support of the prayers in the petition. Referring to Regulation 9(1) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, which permit the filing of application for determination of tariff within 90 days from the actual COD of the unit/ project and the grant of provisional tariff, the learned counsel submitted that the Commission may consider the grant of provisional tariff of Rs.3.24/kWh agreed by beneficiaries, subject to the determination of final tariff. On a query by the Commission, as to why the present petition should be kept pending, keeping in view that the Petitioner is required to file a petition for determination of tariff, based on the COD of the Units and the CEA completion cost, the learned counsel for the Petitioner while seeking permission to withdraw the present petition, sought liberty to approach the Commission for filing the tariff petition, in terms of Regulation 9(1) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, along with its submissions on the approval of R&M for life extension of the project. 7. In view of the above submissions, the present Petition is disposed of as ‘withdrawn’, with liberty to the Petitioner to file the tariff petition for the period from the COD of the units, in terms of Regulation 9(1) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. Liberty is also granted to the Petitioner to seek the reliefs (as in para 1 above), in the said tariff petition to be filed by the Petitioner. The filing fees paid in respect of this petition shall be adjusted in the tariff petition to be filed in terms of the liberty granted as above.
